title: the ...
subtitle: the sun / the same / the police
summary: Learn the groups of words that always take the, and the words that never take it.

lesson.heading: the when there is only one
lesson.text: We use **the** when it is clear which thing or person we mean, because there is only one.

examples.text: What is **the name** of this street? (there is only one name)
Who is **the best player** in your team? (there is only one best player)
Can you tell me **the time**, please? (= the time now)
My office is on **the first floor**.

lesson.heading: Don't forget the
lesson.text: Some phrases sound wrong without **the**. Always say *the city centre* and *the nearest ...*.

examples.text: Do you live near **the city centre**?
Excuse me, where is **the nearest bank**?

lesson.heading: the same ...
lesson.text: **same** always has **the** in front of it.

examples.text: *A:* Are these two books different? *B:* No, they're **the same**.

lesson.heading: We say the with these
rows: the sun / the moon / the world / the sky / the sea / the country
**The sky** is blue and **the sun** is shining.
the police / the fire brigade / the army
My brother is a soldier. He's in **the army**.
the top / the end / the middle / the left / the right
My house is at **the end** of the street.
the piano / the guitar / the trumpet
Paula is learning to play **the piano**.
I listen to **the radio** a lot.
lesson.note: *Do you live in a town or in **the country**?* and *Do you use **the Internet** much?*

lesson.heading: No the with these
lesson.text: We do **not** use *the* with **television/TV**, with **breakfast / lunch / dinner**, or after **next** and **last**.

examples.text: I watch **TV** a lot. What's on **television** tonight?
Did you have a holiday **last summer**?

lesson.text: *What's on television tonight?* = the programmes. But *Can you turn off the television?* = the TV set in this room.

exercises.prompt: The sky is blue and ___ is shining.
exercises.explanation: There is only one sun, so we always say the sun.

exercises.prompt: Emma is sitting on a stool with a musical instrument. She's playing ___.
exercises.explanation: With musical instruments we say the: play the guitar, the piano, the trumpet.

exercises.prompt: It's morning, and the family is eating at the table. They're having ___.
exercises.explanation: No the with breakfast, lunch and dinner.
A building has only one second floor, so we say the second floor.
We do not use the with television when we talk about the programmes.

exercises.statement: Would you like to go to moon?
exercises.explanation: Would you like to go to the moon? There is only one moon.

exercises.prompt: Match each pair of facts with the sentence that says the same thing.

pairs.left: I live in North Street and you live in North Street.
pairs.right: We live in the same street.

pairs.left: I arrived at 8.30 and you arrived at 8.30.
pairs.right: We arrived at the same time.
Jim and Sue are the same age.

pairs.left: My shirt is dark blue and so is my jacket.
pairs.right: My shirt and jacket are the same colour.

pairs.left: I've got no money and you've got no money.

exercises.prompt: Two people are in the water near a big ship. They're swimming in ___.
exercises.explanation: the sea, like the sky and the sun.

exercises.prompt: Somebody was trying to break into the shop, so I called ___.
exercises.explanation: We say the police, the army and the fire brigade.
Japan has only one capital, so we say the capital.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: We live in the country about ten miles from the nearest town.
exercises.explanation: the country = not a town; and we always say the nearest ...
